stories.title: Limoges' town hall spire collapses as France's riots peak
stories.summary: France's Saturday cost-of-living day of action, swelled by the high-school blockade movement that began Sept. 17 at a lycée in Créteil and by former Yellow Vests, turned violent: rioters stormed Marseille's city hall and burned Lyon's tourist office, and around 6 p.m. masked men broke into Limoges' 143-year-old town hall and set it alight. At about 8:30 p.m. local time its 43-meter campanile came down in flames, and Globe Eye News' clip of the collapse got 42K likes, with replies like "We really witnessing a second French Revolution bruh." The Interior Ministry counted 550,000 marchers (organizers said 800,000) and 2,397 arrests, and the BBC later called the ruins the defining image of the protests; fact-checkers flagged older clips, such as cars burning after PSG's Champions League win in May, being passed off as riot footage.
